name: Claude chat
description: Experimental. Runs Claude Code as a chat in a tab instead of a terminal: messages, tool calls and permission prompts as cards, with Enter to send. Open a new chat from the + menu, or move a Claude terminal into one with its Chat badge.

contributes.mcpInstructions: Handing over: to open Claude in another tab or on another account, or give it a session or a task, call claude-chat__open_chat (project, account by name or email, resume a session id or "current", or prompt), or run `wings claude-chat open_chat account=<name>`.

mcpTools.name: open_chat
mcpTools.description: Opens a Claude chat tab in one of the user's projects, under a Claude Code account you name, to hand work over: use it when the user asks to open Claude in another tab, switch account, or give a session or task to another account. Give resume (a session id, or "current" for your own session) to go on with a session, or prompt (up to 8000 characters, for example a handoff summary) to start a new one, not both. A resumed session on another account has its transcript copied there and goes on as a fork by default, so the session you run in stays untouched; fork false goes on with the session itself, only safe when nothing else runs it. The tab opens in the background, and the answer gives its tabId: send_to_agent with it sends the chat a message. Fails, opening nothing, for an unknown project, account or session, or an account that isn't signed in.

project.description: The project's name, folder or id. Leave out for the project you run in.

account.description: The Claude Code account's name or its email, as the chat's account menu shows it, or "default". Leave out for the project's own account.

resume.description: The session id to go on with, or "current" for the session that makes this call. Not with prompt.

prompt.description: The first message of a new session, for example a handoff summary. Not with resume.

fork.description: With resume: go on as a copy, so the original is untouched. True unless you say false.
